body.heading: Words that describe
paragraphs: Some words tell us how something looks or feels: big, tall, fast, happy. These are describing words — grown-ups call them adjectives. And just like actions, describing words love to travel in opposite pairs.
Animals are the best teachers for this chart. Picture each pair as you read!

body.heading: Big and small, tall and short
paragraphs: I am a big elephant. I am a small mouse.
I am a tall giraffe. I am a short rabbit.

body.heading: Fast and slow, happy and sad
paragraphs: I am a fast cheetah. I am a slow snail.
I am a happy monkey. I am a sad monkey. (Same monkey, different day — feelings change, and that is fine.)

body.heading: Heavy and light, wide and narrow… plus two more
paragraphs: I am a heavy hippo. I am a light butterfly.
I am a round pig. I am a thin cat.
Heavy and light are about how much something weighs — a hippo needs a very strong scale, and a butterfly barely needs one at all.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Describe your favorite toy with two describing words — then say their opposites. Does it still sound like your toy?
2. Which pair fits today best: fast or slow? Happy or sad? Hot or cold?

takeaway: Describing words (adjectives) come in opposite pairs — big/small, tall/short, fast/slow, heavy/light — that help us say exactly how things are.
materials: Just you and this page — no materials needed
supervision: A grown-up nearby is recommended for younger readers; the think-and-talk questions work well read aloud together.
